metadata.issued: by the Reserve Bank of Australia as part of the Next Generation Banknote series, and was issued into general circulation on September 20, 2017.

by the Reserve Bank of Australia as part of the Next Generation Banknote series, and was issued into general circulation on October 18, 2018. A typographical error, the last ‘i’ in "responsibility" being missing and spelled instead as "responsibilty", was discovered on earlier print runs of the banknote in May 2019, affecting 46 million banknotes. The Reserve Bank confirmed it was aware of the error since December 2018, and will correct the spelling in later print runs.

metadata.issued: by the Board of Commissioners of Currency, Singapore (since merged to the Monetary Authority of Singapore), as part of the Singapore Portrait Series currency notes, and was issued into general circulation on September 9, 1999. The SG$10,000 and the B$10,000 (of Brunei) are the world's most valuable banknotes (that are officially in circulation) in terms of purchasing power, compared to the other widely used banknote, the 1,000 Swiss francs banknote. On July 2, 2014, the Monetary Authority of Singapore announced that it would stop printing $10,000 notes starting from October 1, 2014, to reduce the risk of money laundering. Singapore has now officially stopped producing the S$10,000 banknote and has thus begun the process of withdrawing it from active circulation. The Monetary Authority of Singapore said that the notes will likely remain legal tender until all the notes slowly get returned as they get damaged.

canada.note: Canada was added only after all circulating coin and banknote denominations had front/back originals and normalized same-size finals.

denmark.note: Banknotes were split from official 2009A combined front/back PNGs. Coins were split from official combined front/back PNGs.

chile.note: Current Chilean banknote and coin front/back images were downloaded from Banco Central de Chile's Billetes y Monedas image index.

costa_rica.note: Current Costa Rican polymer banknotes and BCCR-listed corriente coin designs were downloaded from Banco Central de Costa Rica pages.

uruguay.note: Current Uruguay coin images and BCU banknote combined display images were downloaded from Banco Central del Uruguay subsites.

united_arab_emirates.note: Banknotes were split from official Central Bank of the UAE combined front/back images. Coins were downloaded from official per-side PNGs. The AED 20 note image includes two issue columns; the 2015 right-column front/back images were cropped as the latest issue.

bahrain.note: Downloaded CBB 2023 upgraded fourth issue banknote front/back images and current coin front/back images. WordPress original coin image URLs were used where the page displayed thumbnail variants.

kuwait.note: Downloaded CBK sixth-issue banknote large front/back images. Downloaded CBK current coin 3x combined side images and split each image vertically into front/back originals.

georgia.note: Downloaded National Bank of Georgia current banknote and circulation-coin front/back image files referenced in the Next.js page data.

taiwan.note: Downloaded official CBC Currency Museum detail records and front/back PNG images from /ExhibitsImg/Search/. Images were normalized to matching front/back dimensions per denomination/design.

ukraine.note: Downloaded official National Bank of Ukraine front/back images for current fourth-generation banknotes and legal-tender coins. Images were normalized to matching front/back dimensions per denomination.

morocco.note: Downloaded Bank Al-Maghrib 2023-series banknote front/back reference images. Downloaded 2023-series coin horizontal composite images and split them vertically into front/back originals before normalization.

qatar.note: Downloaded official Qatar Central Bank front/back PNGs for all seven banknote denominations shown on the current-banknotes page. No coins were added in this pass under the partial-coverage inclusion policy.

brunei.note: Downloaded clean official BDCB front/back PNGs for the five 2025-family banknotes now listed on the Currency in Circulation page. The annotated security-feature images and SPECIMEN-marked latest coin image were not used. No coins were added under the partial-coverage inclusion policy.
